scenes.headline: How Carveout turns a splat into labelled 3D objects
scenes.sub: Render its own views, segment them with SAM 3, lift the masks to Gaussians.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Juniper! Carveout takes a trained Gaussian-splat scene and hands back a list of labelled 3D objects. Here's how.

scenes.text: No retraining and no original photos: Carveout renders its own views, segments them, and lifts every 2D mask back onto the Gaussians that drew it.
scenes.say: The idea: no retraining, and no original photos. Carveout renders its own views, segments them, and lifts every mask back onto the Gaussians that drew it.

steps.say: Start from a splat you've trained. Carveout places synthetic cameras inside a volume you approve, and renders its own views.
SAM three runs a confirmed list of noun phrases over every view, and logs every raw score, so the thresholds come from data.
Then the hard part, the lift. Each 2D mask is attributed back to the Gaussians that rendered into it.
Out come objects with position, extents, a box and a confidence. An optional local vision model can confirm, relabel or reject each one.

scenes.title: How the lift settles a disagreement
scenes.say: Say a Gaussian is seen in twenty views. Three say salon chair, one says barber chair, sixteen say nothing. One rule decides.

parts.note: the winning class's alpha-weighted mass, summed over every view
parts.say: Set every colour to one, render, and multiply by the mask. The gradient is each Gaussian's share of the masked pixels. The biggest class total wins.

parts.note: its mass in every view that saw it
parts.say: T is its mass in every view that saw it. A view that detected nothing is a vote against every label.

parts.note: the bar to clear; tuned per class
parts.say: Gamma sets the bar, tuned per class.

scenes.label: per Gaussian per class: the lift's class pass sets the scene ceiling
scenes.note: 30 M Gaussians on a 24 GB card: about 60 classes
scenes.say: The limit is memory. The lift needs about twelve bytes per Gaussian per class, so on a twenty-four gigabyte card, thirty million Gaussians get about sixty classes.

scenes.text: A view votes with the alpha mass the Gaussian has in it: large and frontal counts for more than a sliver.
scenes.say: So each view votes with the mass the Gaussian shows in it. Large and frontal counts for more than a sliver at the edge.

recap: Render its own views, detect with SAM 3
Lift masks by an alpha-weighted vote
About 12 bytes per Gaussian per class
scenes.say: To recap: render, detect, then lift each mask by weighted vote.
